_comment: Olesm Swifttail, Drake [Tactician] / council clerk at the Liscor Guild frontage. Canon (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Olesm_Swifttail): thin, sky-blue-scaled Drake with wildly-patterned blue eyes; earnest, slightly awkward, chess-obsessed, free of the usual Drake prejudices, meticulous with maps and counts; a human once surpassed him at chess and it delighted rather than angered him. The 'resonance' branch is the game's FIRST class-recognition beat -- the hub greeting text_variant gates on classes.tactician (WIDialogue._meets reads _ctx['classes'], id->level; a class gate is visible-but-locked, so a non-Tactician sees the option greyed as a deliberate tease). GH#64: the entry OPTION itself is now skill-gated (`observe`/[Appraise Foe], which Tactician grants at L1) rather than class-gated -- the greeting text_variant stays class-gated on purpose (it recognizes the PC BEING a Tactician, not a skill USE; flagged survivor in the GH#64 audit). C3: the 'cisterns' node is now the Q1 'Something in the Cisterns' GIVER + three-path REPORT hub. The accept option banks heard_about_cisterns (opens the C1 sewer-grate door_when) + starts the `cisterns` quest; cisterns_brief is the explaining beat (what/where/how per onboarding S9). Three report options gate on the path counters (cleared_the_nest / watch_swept_cisterns / scouted_the_nest); the SKILL report ALSO banks resolved_the_cisterns (the other two banked it at resolution time). All bank cisterns_reported + commended_by_olesm (standing) AND pay {gold: 6} -- Olesm the meticulous clerk pays for a finished job / a proper survey ('a map is as good as a corpse to me, and cheaper in bandages'); a coin purse reads right where a physical loot-drop from a clerk would read oddly, so the dialogue {item} effect stays deliberately unused here. Opacity rule: no stats shown; class NAME only; report/quest text carries no counter numerals.

hub.speaker: Olesm
hub.text: Oh — hello. One moment; I'm three columns into a supply tally and if I lose the thread I start again from the granary. ...There. Olesm, council clerk. How can I help?

text_variants.text: Still counting, this late. Someone has to keep the ledger honest after the Council's gone to bed.
Oh — hello. You have the look of someone who counts the exits on the way into a room. A [Tactician]? Truly? I so rarely get to talk shop. Sit, sit. Well. Stand. How can I help?
Still up here? The gallery won't map itself, and I'd rather you were down there with a plan than up here with second thoughts. You have the map. Go.
You climbed back out. I confess I ran the odds while you were down there and did not care for them. Tell me it's over. I have a column that badly wants a number in it.

text_variants._comment: controller voice pass. Issue #80 (world reactivity wave, item 5 -- the news-travels line): seal_kept_report already closes the quest one-off; this is the PERSISTENT hub-greeting reaction (was missing -- only cleared_the_warren had one). Appended LAST (highest priority -- What the Seal Kept resolves chronologically after the raskghar warren).
text_variants.text: The gallery's sealed and the report is filed, which means my column finally has its number. I still don't care for a construct existing under my streets, but I care for it existing under control rather less badly. My thanks, again.

options._comment: GH#64: skill-gated (was class-gated Tactician) -- [Appraise Foe] (a measuring look that reads a room/person/problem) fits reading the city's weak point better than the bare class; Tactician grants it at L1 so every Tactician still opens this branch. The greeting text_variant above stays class-gated deliberately -- it recognizes the PC BEING a Tactician (silhouette/reputation), not a skill USE, so no Skill fits it (flagged survivor, GH#64 audit).
options.text: [Appraise Foe] What's the city's real weak point?
Zevara sent me. The tunnels under the cisterns. What do you have?
It's dead. Zevara's sealing the gallery.
I'll leave you to your tally.

options._comment: stage-2 hub topic, lifted verbatim from docs/design/social-2-staging/olesm_stages.json. Appended AFTER 'I'll leave you to your tally.' (array end) so it can never shift an earlier option's visible index.
options.text: You run half this city from that desk. You know that, right?

options._comment: stage-3 hub topic (⚑ mild canon -- [Strategist] ambition is safe early canon; the letters beat is a proto-newsletter nod kept oblique, never says 'newsletter'). Same array-end index safety.

Issue #25: the chess perk's real payoff (was option+frame only). requires ADDS gold:2 to the existing stage-3 accomplishment leg -- the sanctioned {gold, accomplishment} compound (dialogue.gd's _meets ANDs both; _meets_progress reads only the accomplishment leg, so a met stage with <2 gold shows GREYED, never vanished -- a player who cannot cover the wager's loss side must never be walked into it). hide_when retires the option for good once chess_with_olesm banks (the scene is one-time authored, not a repeatable perk) -- the shorter rematch line in talk_pool_stages is the residue.

FUNCTION: signpost for the bounty_sewer_survey board posting -- its copy (data/bounties.json) names the giver only as 'L. Swifttail, purveyor' and points at 'the east gallery'/'the first junction' with no entrance named, so Olesm (the giver's nephew per that file's giver field) names the sewer-grate entrance in his own voice. Gates ride the bounty lifecycle's real counters: requires accepted_bounty_<id> (WIGame.accept_bounty banks it), hide_when completed_bounty_<id> (WIGame.turn_in_bounty banks it) -- the option exists exactly while the slip is live. Appended at array end so it never shifts an earlier option's visible index.
options.text: Your uncle's board notice — the gallery he means?

options._comment: FUNCTION: the mid-quest re-entry into the cisterns node -- 'You look worried about something.' (above) hides once heard_about_cisterns banks, and this follow-up (requires that same counter, hide_when cisterns_reported) takes over until the report closes the quest; the cisterns node's own text_variants render the correct in-progress/resolved state. CONSTRAINT: dialogue.gd has no text_variants on OPTIONS (node-only), so a state-reflecting hub label must be this multi-option split (briefing/resolution above are the same shape), never a variant on one option. TRAP: QA scripts navigate this hub by cursor index -- cisterns_fight/talk/scout's report phase counts on 'worried' being hidden and this option sitting after the tally exit; re-derive their cursor paths if any gate here changes. Appended at array end for the same index-safety.

8d C1 (issue #14) 'What the Seal Kept' STAGE 1: the stipend accept. Gated on `post_game` (the arc-epilogue completion counter, sleep_veil.gd's own 'ending was witnessed' bank -- the SAME gate erin_errand.json's door-chain beat 1 uses for post-epilogue content) rather than the board rumor above, which is flavor-only; hide_when retires it once accepted (quest completes only via the report option below, never by re-picking this one). Banks the party-counter `horns_delve_started` (the ally_requires gate `warren_mouth`/`gallery_seal_anchor`'s own door_when reads, B3) ALONGSIDE the ADVANCE half of the stipend (5g now, 15g on report -- see `seal_kept_report` below). Appended at array end for the same index-safety every prior hub addition here uses.
options.text: That Watch notice — the gallery survey. I'll take it.

options._comment: 8d C1 (issue #14) 'What the Seal Kept' report beat: gated on `seal_kept_found` (the vault's own post-victory FIND beat), hide_when the completion counter it banks here so re-entry never re-pays. Pays the report half of the stipend (15g) and completes the quest (WIQuests.beat_index reaches beats.size() once seal_kept_reported >= 1). Appended at array end.
options.text: The gallery. It's done — and it's stranger than anyone thought.

olesm_chess_invite.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_invite.text: The board's been out since Tuesday, if you want the honest count. I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Whenever you're ready. I'll even let you have white, which should tell you how confident I am.

olesm_chess_setup.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_setup.text: Not a fresh game, actually. Same position, move for move: my opening, her replies, right up to the moment I stopped seeing straight. Eleven moves in, my bishop's aimed at your king and I am, in my own defense, feeling rather clever about it. Somewhere in here she found a door I didn't. Find it again and I'll believe two people can see the same board the same way.

olesm_chess_puzzle.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_puzzle.text: Here. Your rook's pinned to the corner, my bishop threatens mate in three if you sit still, and I am rather pleased with myself. Two gold on it, friendly, either way. What's the move?

options.text: Trade the rook. Knight takes, clear the corner.
Queen takes the bishop. End the threat now.
Ignore the bishop. Push the pawn, threaten mate in two instead.
Play it safe. Offer the draw.

olesm_chess_wrong_pieces.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_wrong_pieces.text: Safe. Sound. Exactly what I played that day, and exactly why I lost: I traded fear for fear and never once asked what SHE wanted. Try again.

olesm_chess_wrong_queen.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_wrong_queen.text: The obvious answer. Take the piece, kill the threat, sleep well. I made that exact trade against her, three games earlier, and it taught me nothing. Try again.

olesm_chess_win.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_win.text: ...Oh. OH. You'd let the mate stand and walk past it. That's her move. That is EXACTLY her move. I have stared at this position for a season and you found the door in one sitting. I don't know whether to be humiliated or thrilled. Both, I've decided. Here.

olesm_chess_loss.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_loss.text: A draw offered from a winning position is a resignation wearing a hat. I'll take it, and the coin, and I promise to feel appropriately guilty about both. ...Actually, no. Only the first one.

olesm_doubt.speaker: Olesm
olesm_doubt.text: Ha. HA. No. I run the paperwork the Council ignores, and I'm a [Tactician] whose largest engagement to date was a supply-cart dispute. ...Which I won. Decisively. I keep a list of what I'd do if Liscor were ever truly tested. It's a good list. I would just rather die of old age never having to show anyone.

options.text: I hope the list stays theoretical.
The cart never stood a chance.

olesm_doubt_two.speaker: Olesm
olesm_doubt_two.text: So do I. That's the strange arithmetic of the job: you train your whole life for a day you pray never comes, and the better you are, the more boring the city stays. Liscor is very boring. I'm quietly proud of that.

olesm_ambition.speaker: Olesm
olesm_ambition.text: Honestly? There's a class above mine. [Strategist]. Cities write to theirs. Armies wait on them. Some nights I can almost see the shape of the level, like a move you know is on the board and cannot find yet. ...I've started writing to other [Tacticians]. Comparing games, doctrine, mistakes. Perhaps it becomes nothing. Perhaps it becomes something every city wants a copy of.

olesm_ambition_two.speaker: Olesm
olesm_ambition_two.text: You'd be the second subscriber. The first is me, checking for errors. ...Thank you. People ask what I do; you asked what I'm FOR. There's a difference, and it's most of why the second chair stays out.

briefing.speaker: Olesm
briefing.text: I mapped your ledge sketches against the city plans. There's a gallery below the cisterns older than Liscor's walls, and something has been widening it. Kill it, chase it off, or map it — but do NOT let it follow you up. …Take Relc. Please.

resolution.speaker: Olesm
resolution.text: A Raskghar. AWAKE. Under my streets. I'm filing this under 'problems the Council pays adventurers for' — which, as of today, includes you. The seal will hold. Probably. Play chess with me sometime; you've earned the good board.

chess.speaker: Olesm
chess.text: Both sides, yes. It's the only honest way to learn how the enemy thinks. You have to want to win as them. A human beat me across this very board once, so thoroughly I nearly thanked her. I did thank her. Best thing to happen to my game in years.

chess_two.speaker: Olesm
chess_two.text: A loss you understand is worth ten wins you don't. That isn't just chess. That's the whole job. If only the Council read reports the way I read a board.

resonance.speaker: Olesm
resonance.text: The weak point? Everyone points at the gap in the south wall. It isn't. It's that Liscor has never been besieged long enough to learn its own supply. Morale holds until the third hungry week, and no one has ever counted past the second. ...You already knew that. I can see you did. It is, honestly, a relief not to be the only one in the room doing that arithmetic.

resonance_two.speaker: Olesm
resonance_two.text: I would like that. Genuinely. Bring a board. We'll settle the wall and the war in one afternoon.

cisterns.speaker: Olesm
cisterns.text: Worried is the professional term, yes. The market's had reports: things moving under the grates, a cistern gone foul, a fishmonger who swears something looked back at him from the dark. Probably nothing. I do not care for probably-nothings under a walled city. ...Actually. You have the look of someone who finishes things. Would you go down and settle it?

text_variants.text: You're back. The cisterns. Any word? The grate's open now, and whatever's nesting down there will not count itself.
You've the look of someone who's swung a blade recently. The nest under the market. Is it settled? Tell me straight.
Word from the gate says the Watch moved on the cisterns. Was that your doing? I want to hear how it fell out.
You came back with your skin and, unless I misread you, with a picture in your head. You mapped it, didn't you. Show me.
The cisterns are off my ledger and onto the Council's, thanks to you. Quiet streets. I could get used to it.

options.text: I'll look into it. Where do I start?
It's dealt with. I cleared the nest myself.
The Watch swept it. Captain Zevara's people handled it.
I didn't fight it. I mapped it: the nest, the count, the exits. [Appraise Foe]
Let me know if it turns into a something.

cisterns_brief.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_brief.text: Thank you. Here's what I have. What: something's nested in the old cisterns under the market. The reports say spiders, big ones, silver-backed, the kind that climb up from the Dungeon when a wall cracks. Where: down the green sewer-grate off the south square. It's rusted, but it'll open now that someone official wants it open. How: I genuinely don't mind. Put a blade through it, get the Watch to sweep it, or just bring me a proper picture of what's down there — count, size, exits. A map is as good as a corpse to me, and cheaper in bandages. Settle it however suits you, then come tell me it's done.

cisterns_done.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_done.text: Then it's over, and the city's quieter for it. That's real work, the kind nobody thanks you for, so let me be the exception. You've the Council's gratitude, and mine, which comes with more paperwork but rather more warmth. If you ever want a game, or a job that needs a clear head, you know where the board is.

cisterns_intel.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_intel.text: ...Oh, this is lovely work. You counted them. Exits, chokepoints, the drop where the tunnel falls away. The whole shape of the problem on one page. Now the Watch goes in knowing the ground instead of bleeding to learn it. A map IS as good as a corpse, and I have never once gotten to say that to someone who agreed. Take the Council's thanks — and mine, doubled, because you did it the clever way.

lism_errand.speaker: Olesm
lism_errand.text: My uncle's notice? That's the same gallery under the cisterns — down the green sewer-grate off the south square, same as I'd send you for the nest. He wants two things confirmed in writing: the old drainage marker, still legible or not, and whether the phosphor moss has spread past the first junction. Both, mind. He does not deal in 'probably.'

seal_survey_offer.speaker: Olesm
seal_survey_offer.text: The Watch wants eyes on the reopened gallery — proper eyes, not another guardsman who reports 'it is dark.' Five gold now, fifteen when you bring me something I can put in a report. The Guild is sending a Silver-rank team to meet you there.

seal_kept_report.speaker: Olesm
seal_kept_report.text: A construct, a vault, and ANOTHER rune-door. Do you know what this does to my casualty projections? ...Nothing good. Here is your fifteen. Earned.
